facts.text: Conchas Dam was completed in 1939, costing $15.8 million, and is a concrete gravity main section 1,250 feet long and 200 feet high.
The reservoir created by Conchas Dam holds 259,000 acre‑feet for conservation and irrigation, with an additional 198,000 acre‑feet reserved for flood control.
Conchas Dam sits just downstream from where the South Canadian and Conchas Rivers meet, about 35 miles northwest of Tucumcari.
The dam’s construction began in the early 1930s as part of a New Deal effort to bring water management and jobs to the Southwest.
Conchas Lake offers a 9‑hole golf course, camping, and picnic facilities, all managed by the State of New Mexico Park and Recreation Division.
The dam’s 3,000‑foot concrete emergency spillway lies north of the main structure, while a 300‑foot service spillway sits within the dam itself.
